$comment: The App Store privacy nutrition label and age rating, as data.
THIS FILE IS AN ATTESTATION. docs/STORE-FORMS.md is its prose twin and
carries the reasoning for every value here; read that before approving
this, because what you are approving is a legal statement about what
the app collects. scripts/asc-push.mjs transcribes it — it does not
decide it. The ageRating block below it PUSHES; the privacy rows it
PRINTS as the web form, in the order App Store Connect asks, because
Apple's API has no App Privacy resource to write to (D73).
Why a file and not the web form: the form is ~40 clicks that have to
agree with docs/data-inventory.md, and nothing checks that they do.
Here the answers are reviewable in a diff, and check:store-forms holds
them equal to STORE-FORMS.md so the two cannot drift.
If you disagree with a value, change it HERE and in STORE-FORMS.md.
Changing it in App Store Connect instead is worse for the two halves in
different ways: the next age-rating push silently reverts you, and the
privacy label simply drifts from this file with nothing noticing —
which is the failure this file was created to prevent.

tracking.$why: No IDFA, no ATT prompt, no advertising SDK. The Facebook SDK is a transitive SwiftPM dependency of @capacitor-firebase/authentication and is stripped at postinstall (D16); check:ios-facebook asserts its absence. Every collected row below is therefore NOT_USED_FOR_TRACKING.

collected.$why: The Firebase uid. Anonymous by default (D3) — every install becomes one at first paint. ALSO THE HANDLE since D122 (v2_users/{uid}.handle, plus the v2_handles registry keyed by the name): user-chosen, unique, and readable by any signed-in user. Apple's own definition of this type names it — 'any screen name, handle, account ID …' — so the handle lands in the row that was already Yes and the ANSWER does not move. The basis for it did, which is why this line says so: a row whose stated reason is stale is the D116 failure one layer in, and a future contributor deciding whether this row still holds reads this sentence.

Only if the user links Google. linkGoogle() calls new GoogleAuthProvider() with no addScope (src/lib/firebaseImpl.ts:167) and Firebase requests email and profile by default, so the auth record holds it. No Firestore document of ours does — but the form asks what is collected.

Optional display name, shown beside every answer, take and reveal — since D98 answers are public and attributed, so this is the label the whole app renders people under. Also arrives from Google's default profile scope. An account that sets none renders as 'Someone'.

Answers and test results. Since D98 these are READABLE BY ANY SIGNED-IN USER, under the author's display name and with the age band, gender, city, country and education the answer was given under. That is the product, not a leak; the form asks what is collected, and this row was already Yes.

City name only. The fix is resolved to a city on the device (src/v2/data/locate.ts) and discarded, so no coordinate is ever transmitted — but a city name is still coarse location data, and under-declaring is the direction that gets an app pulled. NEVER add PRECISE_LOCATION: iOS sets NSLocationDefaultAccuracyReduced and never calls requestTemporaryFullAccuracy, so it is unobtainable by construction rather than by policy.

The politics test result is GDPR Art. 9 special-category data; gender if entered. STAYS DECLARED, and the justification changed at D98: it is no longer true that this never leaves the owner document. Political ITEM answers are public and now slice by cohort like every other question (D98 reversed D44), and the politics RESULT vector sits on a profile any signed-in user may read. The row was Yes before because the form asks what you collect; it is Yes now for that reason and because the app also publishes it. Deleting this row would be an under-declaration and check-store-forms rule 2 refuses it.

Sentry. On by default with an opt-out in the privacy panel (D76), carries the uid only — no email, no name, no session replay, sendDefaultPii: false. Was a Yes even while opt-in: the form asks what the app CAN collect.

notCollected.$why: Recorded so a reviewer's question has an answer and so a future contributor sees which absences were decided rather than forgotten. Three of these look tickable and are not:
notCollected.DEVICE_ID: Device binding (D29) receives 2-3 bits from Apple DeviceCheck meaning 'an account was activated from this device recently'. The server stores no device identifier; the platforms hold the state. There is nothing for deleteAccount to erase because nothing is held.
notCollected.PRODUCT_INTERACTION: data-inventory.md: no product analytics of any kind ship today. Adding any would change this row.
notCollected.EMAILS_OR_TEXT_MESSAGES: Still No, and still for the shape reason: a take is a POST — to a circle (D78 part 1) or, since D83, anonymously to the world — never a message to a person, and Apple files posts under User Content > Other User Content, which is already declared Yes above. So the CONTENT is declared either way and this row is about shape. It moves if a direct person-to-person surface ships. The age rating did move — messagingAndChat is true (D79) — because that question asks whether the app has chat at all rather than what category the text lands in, and the two forms genuinely diverge here. D122's circle INVITATION is the first thing to test that trigger, and it does not trip it — checked against the write rather than the feature name: inviteToGroupV2 sets to, from, fromName, groupName, mode and at, and there is NO free-text field for a sender to write into. An invitation is a capability offered to one person, not a message sent to them. It would move this row the day an invite carries a note.

ageRating.$why: Every content frequency question is NONE, measured rather than assumed: scanning all four committed banks for violence, sex, substances, gambling and profanity returns four hits, all references rather than depictions — 'Pub' as a place option, 'Cry in a film', an etymology card for the word alcohol, and a history card naming the Second World War. Re-run that scan if the banks grow substantially (the farm, D33, writes the spec layer; promotion, D30, is the gate where new content reaches users).
ageRating.$new2025: The eight below are Apple's newer questions — the ones $socialMediaQuestions predicted. They are REQUIRED: omitting them makes the PATCH 409 with 'You must provide a value for the attribute …', naming each one (D75). Types are Apple's: seven booleans and one frequency enum, taken from the App Store Connect OpenAPI spec rather than inferred from the field names.
ageRating.$userGeneratedContent: Yes, and it is the one that actually drives the rating. Group and duel reveals show display names — user-generated content on any version of this form, whatever the content answers say. STORE-FORMS.md structural fact 1.
ageRating.$messagingAndChat: YES since 2026-08-09 (D79), and it was false for one day. D78 part 1 shipped the circle takes client — postTake writes free text that other members of the group read — so the second half of the old reasoning ('demo-only in a shipping build') expired the moment it merged. Scope limits the AUDIENCE, not the feature: Apple asks whether the app has messaging or chat, and a private group where members write to each other is chat — all the more so now that takes also exist at world scale (D83, anonymous). Under-declaring is the direction that pulls an app, and the honest answer costs nothing here — the rating is already driven to 12+ by userGeneratedContent. D78's cost table filed this flip under its world-takes part; D79 settled it early in the safer direction, and D83 then shipped the part it was filed under.
ageRating.$advertising: No ad SDK of any kind. The Facebook SDK arrives only as a transitive SwiftPM dependency of @capacitor-firebase/authentication and is stripped at postinstall (D16); check:ios-facebook asserts its absence on every CI run.
ageRating.$lootBox: No in-app purchases at all, so nothing randomised to sell. MONETIZATION.md records no consumer paid tier at launch.
ageRating.$parentalControls: The app ships none. This asks what the app PROVIDES, not what it needs — answering yes without the feature is the over-declaration direction.
ageRating.$ageAssurance: No age verification or estimation mechanism. Anonymous-first auth (D3) collects no birth date and nothing gates on age.
ageRating.$healthOrWellnessTopics: Measured across all five committed banks, not assumed: three hits, none of them health content. 'Medicine' is one of four options on "Humanity's best invention?"; the other two are Map taxonomy — CAT_META's Body category carries seedId 'health' for its palette hue, and one cuisine question files under ['Body','Health']. A category label is not a health topic. The nearest real candidate is the personality and politics profiles, and neither is health or wellness. Re-run the scan if the banks grow substantially, on the same trigger as the content scan above.
ageRating.$gunsOrOtherWeapons: Measured across all five committed banks for gun, rifle, pistol, firearm, weapon, knife, sword, bomb, shoot, ammo, bullet, blade, dagger, missile and grenade: ZERO hits. A frequency enum rather than a boolean, so NONE rather than false — the type came from Apple's spec, because guessing boolean here is a 400 that reads like a wrong value.
ageRating.$structural: These three are what actually drive the rating, and they are structural rather than content facts: users see each other's display names in group and duel reveals (user-generated content and social interaction on any version of this form, whatever the content answers say); coarse location exists and is optional (D9); and free text is LIVE at BOTH scopes — circle-scoped with names since D78 part 1 (2026-08-09), and world-scale WITHOUT names since D83 (2026-08-10): anonymous takes, one per person per question, behind enforced moderation (MOD_ADVISORY=false). The fact this form answers from has moved twice: from 'no live free-text surface' to 'circle-scoped' (D79) to 'both scopes, world anonymous' (D83).
ageRating.$expect: 12+ / 13+. Answer it deliberately rather than accepting a default.
ageRating.$socialMediaQuestions: ANSWERED — the eight $new2025 keys above are those questions. This note predicted them (banner seen 2026-08-07) and correctly predicted that asc-push would leave anything new UNSET, but it was wrong about the consequence in a way worth keeping: it said an unset required field 'blocks submission'. Apple is stricter than that — it rejects the whole PATCH with a 409 per missing attribute, so the age rating could not be written at all until every one was supplied (D75). A prediction that is right about the cause and wrong about the symptom still costs a debugging round. The three structural facts below are what these turn on. The free-text one has moved twice (see $structural); since D83 there IS a world-scale surface, and what answers guideline 1.2 for it is the full kit: enforced moderation, report, per-author mute, anonymity by construction — not absence.
ageRating.$guideline12: 1.2 demands four things of any app with user-generated content, and each has a real answer. FILTERING: the moderation substrate is deployed and ENFORCING since D83 (MOD_ADVISORY = false, a remove verdict really hides, a per-run cap bounds a bad run). REPORTING: live since D78 part 1 — flagTake writes to v2_flags from the takes panel, and since D98 any signed-in user may flag any take at either scope, because reading is no longer membership-gated. BLOCKING: this answer was re-derived at D98 and is now ONE shape rather than two. It used to be 'leave the circle, or hide the author', on the reasoning that circle members were the only NAMED people whose content you saw. D98 makes every take named at world scale, so leaving a circle no longer bounds who you see — the real, universal control is the per-author mute (Hide author, data/mutes.ts, local and silent), which applies at both scopes and is what a reviewer should be pointed at. Leaving a circle remains available and still stops that circle's content, but it is no longer the block. CONTACT: olaftaule01@gmail.com on web/terms.html.
